extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIH K99/R00 career-development grants
extracted.subtask_description: Practical resource list and checklist for preparing and submitting an NIH K99/R00 (Pathway to Independence) grant application, including required application components, forms, FOA-specific rules, and suggested explanatory videos and blog posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the specific FOA
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for agency specific FOA. Make sure to follow specific FOA per your research domain and funding agency under which you are applying K99/R00 grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissuance of FOA and other important announcements, check subsection Related Notices. The FOA contains application-specific instructions and requirements—use it as the authoritative source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct forms (SF424 R&R version)
rubrics_metrics.description: SF424 R&R for K grants - Checkout FOA and ask your grants coordinator to find the applicable version. I used Version F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you submit using the SF424 R&R form/version specified by the FOA and institutional grants office; mismatched forms can invalidate or delay submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Page limits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the page limits specified in the FOA and the SF424 instructions; check the formatting guide for allowed fonts, margins, and page-count rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: formatting guide
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the formatting guide to comply with font, margin, line-spacing, and file-type requirements; incorrect formatting can cause pages to be counted incorrectly or sections to be noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Review Criteria & Scoring for K99/R00
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Criteria & Scoring K99/R00
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the FOA's review criteria and any NIH guidance on scoring for K99/R00—understand how reviewers evaluate significance, investigator, innovation, approach, environment, and career-development components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check Application Review Information subsection
rubrics_metrics.description: Check subsection Application Review Information in FOA. This subsection has detailed information of review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Application Review Information subsection usually explains how reviewers will assess the application and lists review criteria—use it to align your proposal with reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required administrative and compliance sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover page etc.; Facilities; Equipment; Biosketch PI; Biosketch Mentors; Current and Pending Support for Mentors; Budget; Budget Justification; Institutional Environment; Institutional Commitment; Vertebrate Animals Section; Human Subjects Section; Resource Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each listed administrative/compliance section required by the FOA is present and complete; missing or incomplete compliance sections can cause administrative rejection or reviewer concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare science and career-development narrative components
rubrics_metrics.description: Science: Project Summary or Abstract; Project Narrative; Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Training in RCR; References; Authentication of Key Resources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These scientific and career-development sections must clearly state aims, significance, approach, and the candidate's development plan; include training in responsible conduct of research and resource authentication as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain statements and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement from Mentor, Co-mentor; Letters of Support - Advisory Committee, Collaborators; Letters of recommendation - Referees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect mentor statements, collaborator/advisory letters, and referee recommendations that specifically address the candidate's potential, mentorship quality, and the feasibility/support for the transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document candidate's career-development plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, feasible career-development plan with measurable milestones toward independence; reviewers evaluate the quality of training and likelihood of career advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clear Specific Aims page
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a concise Specific Aims page that frames the problem, states objectives/hypotheses, and previews the research and career-development plan—this is critical for reviewer first impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a rigorous Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present rationale, preliminary data (if any), detailed methods, potential pitfalls and alternatives, and timeline; align the research with the candidate's training goals and independence plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in RCR
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a plan for RCR training as required by the FOA; describe format, content, and frequency of RCR activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Authentication of Key Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of Key Resources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how key biological/chemical resources will be validated and authenticated to ensure reproducibility, per NIH guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand scoring mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring - How does it work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn how NIH scoring (e.g., 1–9 scale, criterion scores, overall impact) and summary statements work so you can target the elements that drive score and overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch recommended NIH videos and webinars
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write successful K99 grant; Writing an 'effective' K application; Grantsmanship for Postdocs; Demystifying the K99/R00 Application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author suggests watching at least two NIH officer videos (Michael K. Schmidt and P. Kay Lund) and other webinars to hear PO and reviewer perspectives—these supplement written guidance and highlight common pitfalls/advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates for Specific Aims, Research Plan, CDP, and Mentor Plan from Grant Writing Staff at Purdue University
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutionally provided templates and exemplar applications (specific aims, research plan, career development plan, mentor plan) to structure documents and ensure required headings/content are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read blog posts and applicant/reviewer commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Blog posts/threads: detailed guides and experience reports (e.g., Anita Devineni, Mathew Kiang, Elizabeth Brunk, Jordan Ward, Tim Stuart, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult experienced applicants' blog posts for practical tips, timelines, common mistakes, and reviewer insights—but always cross-check with the official FOA/instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow timelines and create a submission plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured timeline for K99 (example resources listed)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use suggested timelines to schedule drafting, mentor input, institutional approvals, and submission well before the deadline to allow for revisions and institutional processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: When in doubt, contact program staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Q&A about grants - When in Doubt, Reach Out!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear about FOA interpretation, eligibility, or review expectations, contact the NIH program officer or your institutional grants coordinator for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify related notices and FOA updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Check subsection Related Notices for reissuance of FOA and other important announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor Related Notices to catch reissued FOAs, policy changes, or application extensions that could affect your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult grantsmanship resources and experienced reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantsmanship resources (e.g., NIH podcasts, DrugMonkey posts, tweetorials) and webinars with reviewers and POs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn grantsmanship principles from NIH officers and experienced reviewers—understanding how reviewers think can improve clarity, significance, and approach sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examples from related NIH mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a research plan - NIAID (example RO1 from a new investigator) and Quick guide for grant applicants by NIAAA, NIH
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, consult example research plans from related NIH institutes and mechanisms to adapt structure and level of detail appropriate for your research and career stage.
